item.title: Man caught red-handed stealing €4,000 from Mrieħel warehouse
item.description: A 59-year-old man from San Ġwann was arrested on Saturday night after police caught him inside a warehouse on Triq l-Intornjatur, Mrieħel, in the limits of Birkirkara. Officers found a smashed window facing the parking area, and during a search recovered gloves, a saw and pliers along with a pouch holding about €4,000 in cash, allegedly taken from a forced drawer. He is being held at the Floriana police lock-up pending investigations and is expected to be arraigned in court in coming days.

item.title: Comino's famous roofless cave collapses; no one injured
item.description: A large section of Popeye's Cave, known in Maltese as L-Għar ta' Bla Saqaf near Crystal Lagoon, collapsed on Sunday morning, leaving huge boulders blocking much of its entrance. The Civil Protection Department confirmed nobody was injured and that officers cordoned off the area, while boat operator Outdoor Explorers Malta placed the rockfall at around 9.30am to 9.40am. The ERA is examining the circumstances and the cause has yet to be established, four months after a natural limestone arch near Santa Marija Battery collapsed onto a jet ski and killed a tourist.

item.title: Malta Police honour fallen officers and war heroes on Remembrance Day
item.description: The Malta Police Force held wreath-laying ceremonies at the Police Graves within the Addolorata Cemetery before joining the national Remembrance Day ceremony in Valletta. Officers paid respects to departed colleagues who served the force and to those who lost their lives serving the country, particularly during war. The force said the commemorations honoured the dedication and sacrifice of those being remembered.

item.title: 'I've never seen the building so full': TCN community blood drive fills the blood bank
item.description: Dozens of people turned up for a blood drive organised by the Indian community and the General Workers Union at the Pietà blood bank on Sunday. Director of Malta's blood donation services Monique Debattista said she had "never seen the blood donation centre so full", calling the initiative a success. GWU general secretary Kevin Camilleri said most Maltese understand the positive contribution TCNs make to Malta, while the drive follows controversial Budget 2027 measures that will see TCNs face new fees for staying, transport and childcare.

item.title: Almost 70% of Malta's economic growth driven by workforce expansion, Alex Borg warns
item.description: Opposition leader Alex Borg said almost 70% of Malta's 82% increase in gross value added between 2015 and 2025 came from adding workers, against just 3% from productivity. Citing government and Chamber of Commerce figures, Borg said productivity growth fell from 2.2% in 2023 to 0.2% in 2024 and turned negative in 2025. He set out four challenges — productivity, skills shortages, wages and tourism — and warned that 17% of the population is at risk of poverty.

item.title: President Spiteri Debono visits Maltese child receiving specialist treatment in London
item.description: President Myriam Spiteri Debono visited Great Ormond Street Hospital in London, where she met a three-year-old Maltese child undergoing treatment for a serious medical condition. The child has been receiving specialised care in the UK for around three months and is expected to need several more months of treatment outside Malta. The President's office said the visit underlined the importance of organisations such as the Malta Community Chest Fund in supporting patients and the relatives who accompany them abroad. The President also visited the Franciscan Sisters' residence of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in London, which hosts Maltese patients and their families during treatment.

item.title: One of Malta's last surviving Punic towers to be restored in Żurrieq
item.description: The Planning Commission has approved the restoration of the Domus Curialis in Żurrieq and the opening of the locality's parish house to the public. The Grade II scheduled complex on Misraħ ir-Repubblika, built before 1967, houses in its rear garden a Class A archaeological site: a quadrangular Punic tower from the late 6th century BC, the only surviving structure of its height remaining in Malta and Sicily. The old parish meeting hall and choir club will be converted into a permanent exhibition space and a community kitchen.

item.title: Tributes pour in for former Franciscan friar Fr Adrijanu Cachia
item.description: Band clubs and organisations across Malta paid tribute to the former Franciscan friar Fr Adrijanu Cachia, who died on Thursday at the age of 80, known for his social work and involvement in village feasts. Several societies recalled him as a benefactor and spiritual director, including Soċjetà Mużikali San Ġużepp Ħamrun and Soċjetà Filarmonika Lourdes Qrendi, which he served for more than 40 years. A final farewell is scheduled for 10 November at 8.30am at the Santa Marija ta' Ġesu church in Rabat.

item.title: Momentum calls on Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg to resign over prosecution failures
item.description: Momentum has urged Attorney General Victoria Buttigieg to resign, citing the acquittals in the trials of the Daphne Caruana Galizia and Lassana Cisse murders and the prosecution blunders in the case of Maximilian Ciantar. Party executive member Matthew Agius said recurring shortcomings in criminal prosecutions undermine Malta's justice institutions, weaken public confidence in safety and security, and demoralise police officers. Momentum is also pressing the government to strengthen the Prosecution Unit with better pay, staffing and career progression, and to introduce a transparent revolving-door framework between the prosecution office and private legal practice.

item.title: 25,000 sqm of abandoned land in Ħal Għaxaq regenerated as picnic and recreation zone
item.description: An area of around 25,000 square metres in Triq l-Andar, Ħal Għaxaq, abandoned for years, has been regenerated into a picnic and recreation zone by Project Green with an investment of over €1 million. The site was officially inaugurated by Environment Minister Miriam Dalli in the presence of Ħal Għaxaq mayor Karl Boxall. It preserves more than 500 existing olive trees and includes public facilities, a cycling area and a children's playground, plus a 60-cubic-metre rainwater catchment reservoir used for irrigation.

item.title: Archbishop Scicluna: no one is a third-class human being
item.description: Archbishop Charles J Scicluna used his Remembrance Day homily at St John's Co-Cathedral to urge respect and dignity for third-country nationals in Malta, two weeks after Budget 2027 announced measures hitting non-EU workers. He said a person may be classified as a TCN in the eyes of the law but no one is a third-class human being in the eyes of God. The Archbishop drew parallels with the thousands of foreign servicemen buried in Malta and with Maltese emigrants of the post-war era, and stressed that while countries have the right to regulate migration, legal status should never diminish fundamental dignity.

item.title: Chamber of Advocates backs an 'open-minded' review of Malta's jury system
item.description: The Chamber of Advocates said it would support a properly constituted commission to review Malta's jury system, provided the exercise is conducted with a genuinely "open-minded" remit and is not driven by a predetermined conclusion. The Chamber's comments come as a petition advocating the abolition of jury trials, first launched on 15 September 2026, has regained attention following the verdict in the murder of Lassana Cisse. It said a review should be free to examine both the strengths of the system and areas needing improvement.

item.title: Is AI behind redundancies in Malta's iGaming sector?
item.description: Malta's iGaming industry is going through a period of adjustment: despite strong economic performance and continued demand for skilled professionals, reports of job losses have raised concerns about employment in one of the country's largest industries. Some former employees claim AI systems are replacing workers in marketing, content creation and design, while industry representatives point to tax pressures, regulatory costs and changing market conditions. The MGA said the locally licensed gaming sector generated €1.422 billion in value added.

item.title: The racist hit-and-run that still haunts May Malimi
item.description: Nearly eight years after May Malimi was left unconscious with a fractured collarbone in a racially motivated hit-and-run in Birżebbuġa, the 24-year-old says he is still afraid to go outside. Malimi was grievously injured in February 2019; former soldier Lorin Scicluna was jailed this week for eight years, with the judge saying the court wanted to warn against racial hatred. Malimi remains scarred by the attack and by the earlier acquittal of Scicluna in the murder of Lassana Cisse.

item.title: Libya guarantees Lilu King will not be executed if extradited
item.description: Libya has guaranteed that Mohamed Ali Elmushraty, better known as Lilu King, will not be executed or tortured if he is extradited from Malta to face murder and drug trafficking charges. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the necessary documents have been received, so the evaluation of the extradition request can begin. Justice Minister Clifton Grima said he would authorise proceedings as soon as legal requirements are met, with the courts ultimately deciding whether extradition can proceed.

item.title: Caruana: 'Labour shelved my 300-page warning on population growth'
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said he warned his own government as early as 2018 about the strains population growth would place on housing, hospitals, schools and roads, but that the roughly 300-page report was never acted on. He said he later raised public alarm in June 2023 by warning Malta could reach 800,000 people by 2040. The remarks came after former minister Evarist Bartolo claimed Caruana's advice was ignored when he was Jobsplus CEO.

item.title: Super bonus pledge drove a higher tourist tax increase than planned
item.description: Government had initially told the Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association that the eco-contribution would rise to around €5 or €6, with the additional revenue financing the super bonus. According to sources, Prime Minister Robert Abela insisted the super bonus be paid in full, prompting a further increase in the tourist tax in Budget 2027. The higher eco-contribution is expected to generate €214 million, and the accommodation sector is now scrambling for solutions.

item.title: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana rules out changes to Budget 2027 measures for non-EU workers
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said the Budget 2027 measures affecting non-EU workers are, apart from some cosmetic changes, "set in stone" as far as he is concerned, as Labour officials, MPs and unions lobby for concessions. Government and the General Workers' Union have been pressing for more humane treatment of third-country nationals under the announced measures.

item.title: Maltese artist brings animals to life using recycled metal in new Ta' Qali exhibition
item.description: A Maltese artist has opened a new exhibition in Ta' Qali that brings animal figures to life using discarded and recycled metal. The show continues the local art scene's run of environmentally themed exhibitions in the village and offers visitors an unusual look at how scrap material can be turned into sculptural work.
